senses.definition: The layer that translates raw tables into the business terms everyone agrees on.
senses.caution: It sounds like plumbing and is really governance. The build is the easy half; the hard half is getting three departments to agree what an active client is, so promising a sponsor one by Q3 is promising to win an argument you have not had yet. Do not stretch it to mean any abstraction or any API either: people who have built one hear a specific piece of the stack and will price and staff it accordingly.
senses.example: Two dashboards disagree on churn because each defines it in its own SQL. That is exactly what a semantic layer is for.

cues.text: Finance and operations arrive at the same meeting with two different revenue numbers, and both are correct against their own queries.
A director asks why self-service reporting keeps producing figures nobody trusts, and you want to name the missing piece between the warehouse and the dashboards.
You are costing a data platform and need a line item for the component that holds the business definitions in one place instead of in every tool separately.

distractors: The underlying layer everything above it runs on and takes for granted.
A basic building block a platform hands you and expects you to compose with.
An isolated environment where code runs without touching anything real.
A slice of the market defined by the industry it serves, such as banking or logistics.
One of the handful of cloud providers that runs compute and storage at planetary scale.
